scorecard.note: Provide verifiable data sources and simplify the visual of the mercury column so it clearly illustrates the temperature drop on a phone screen.

storyboard.ears: The familiar normal temperature hides both biological change and measurement error.
Men born in the 1990s average 97.5 degrees. Body temperature is lower than the historic figure.
storyboard.evidence: Stanford Medicine | Average US body temperature by birth era | https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2020/01/human-body-temperature-has-decreased-in-united-states.html | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: Men's average temperature fell 1.06 degrees. The decline was larger than the one measured in women.
storyboard.eyes: substance: the red mercury column; cause: Data pours ice water over each bulb and the column drops, the men's twice as far
storyboard.evidence: Stanford Medicine | Body temperature decline by sex, 1800s to today | https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2020/01/human-body-temperature-has-decreased-in-united-states.html | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: The original figure recalculates to 98.2 degrees. Measurement also explains why the old standard no longer fits.
storyboard.evidence: JAMA (Journal of the American Medical Association) | Wunderlich's original 98.6F figure vs its 1992 recalculation | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Mackowiak+critical+appraisal+98.6 | 2026-11-12

storyboard.ears: One historic number cannot capture how normal body temperature varies and changes.
